triples.head: DNA polymerase
triples.evidence: The addition of nucleotides requires energy; this energy is obtained from the nucleoside triphosphates dATP, dGTP, dTTP and dCTP.

triples.head: DNA polymerase III
triples.evidence: DNA pol III is the enzyme required for DNA synthesis; DNA pol I is an important accessory enzyme in DNA replication, and along with DNA pol II, is primarily required for repair.

triples.head: DNA polymerase I
triples.evidence: DNA pol I is an important accessory enzyme in DNA replication, and along with DNA pol II, is primarily required for repair.

triples.head: Helicase
triples.evidence: An enzyme called helicase unwinds the DNA by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the nitrogenous base pairs.

triples.head: Primase
triples.evidence: Another enzyme, RNA primase, synthesizes an RNA segment that is about five to ten nucleotides long and complementary to the template DNA.

triples.head: DNA ligase
triples.evidence: The nicks that remain between the newly synthesized DNA (that replaced the RNA primer) and the previously synthesized DNA are sealed by the enzyme DNA ligase.

triples.head: DNA polymerase
triples.evidence: It also requires a free 3'-OH group to which it can add nucleotides by forming a phosphodiester bond between the 3'-OH end and the 5' phosphate of the next nucleotide.

triples.head: DNA polymerase
triples.evidence: DNA polymerase can now extend this RNA primer, adding nucleotides one-by-one that are complementary to the template strand.

triples.head: Topoisomerase
triples.evidence: Topoisomerase prevents the over-winding of the DNA double helix ahead of the replication fork as the DNA is opening up.

triples.head: DNA polymerase
triples.evidence: Only one new DNA strand, the one that is complementary to the 3' to 5' parental DNA strand, can be synthesized continuously towards the replication fork.

triples.head: DNA polymerase
triples.evidence: The other strand, complementary to the 5' to 3' parental DNA, is extended away from the replication fork, in small fragments known as Okazaki fragments.

triples.head: DNA polymerase I

triples.head: DNA polymerase III

triples.head: DNA polymerase I
triples.evidence: The gaps are filled by DNA pol I by adding dNTPs.

triples.head: DNA ligase
triples.evidence: DNA ligase, which catalyzes the formation of phosphodiester linkages between the 3'-OH end of one nucleotide and the 5' phosphate end of the other fragment.
